How to read a file — Rust FAQ

www.rustfaq.org/en/how-to-read-a-file/
Use std::fs::File combined with std::io::BufReader to read the file in chunks or line by line. Streaming the data keeps memory usage constant regardless of file size. Path flexibility. read_to_string accepts any type that implements AsRef<Path>. You can pass a &str, a String, a &Path, or a PathBuf. The compiler converts these types automatically.

Read_to_string () Function vs read_to_string () Method

users.rust-lang.org/t/read-to-string-function-vs-read-to-string-method/39582
The read_to_string function on the Read trait (which File implements) returns the number of bytes read on success in the ok variant. As for returning a String, yes that would also be possible, but the current design allows reuse of an existing allocation.

Deep Dive into Rust's std::fs::read_to_string () Function

betanet.net/view-post/deep-dive-into-rust-s-std-fs-read_to_str
The std::fs::read_to_string () function is responsible for reading the entire contents of a specified file and converting it into a single String data type. It is essential for applications that require reading text files easily, whether for configuration, data processing, or logging.
